drhp.business: Vraj Iron and Steel operates two integrated steel manufacturing facilities in Chhattisgarh (Bilaspur and Raipur), producing Sponge Iron, MS Billets and TMT Bars with captive power and solar power generation for captive consumption. The integrated model allows captive use of intermediate products and power, and the Company primarily caters to the infrastructure, construction, engineering and allied sectors.
drhp.expansion: During FY 2025-26 the Company commissioned a 153,000 MTPA MS Billet Plant (commercial production from 27 March 2026) and a 15 MW Captive Power Plant (commissioned 18 December 2025) at its Bilaspur facility, along with a 15 MW Solar Power Plant. For FY 2026-27 the Company proposes to expand TMT Bar manufacturing capacity by 150,000 MTPA and Captive Power generation capacity by 21 MW, and has approved setting up an additional 21 MW Solar Power Plant expected to be completed and commissioned during FY 2026-27, plus a Rolling Mill at Bilaspur for TMT Bars with installed capacity of 150,000 TPA. The Company also proposes a first-stage Greenfield Integrated Steel Project at Bastar, Chhattisgarh comprising a Sponge Iron Plant (201,000 TPA), MS Billet Plant (201,000 TPA), and two power plants (WHRB 15 MW, CFBC 15 MW), citing proximity to iron ore resources, improved logistics and Chhattisgarh government industrial-policy incentives for the Bastar region.

sk.overview: India is the world's second-largest crude steel producer and second-largest stainless-steel consumer/third-largest producer, with estimated installed SS capacity of 6.6-6.8 Mn tons. Stainless steel is a high-alloy, corrosion-resistant value-added steel (>10.5% chromium) used across railways, process industries, kitchenware, automotive, construction and infrastructure. Long and flat steel demand is closely tied to overall economic, industrial and consumer activity; the sector is raw-material (SS scrap, nickel, chromium) and energy intensive and prices are volatile.

demand_drivers.title: Mdna (RHP)
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian steel demand expected to remain robust, driven by urbanisation, industrialisation, renewable energy investments and continued public infrastructure spending
- Government imposed a 12% safeguard duty on certain categories of steel imports during the year, providing partial protection against low-priced imports and supporting domestic steel prices
- Commissioning of additional Sponge Iron and MS Billet capacity expected to contribute to higher production volumes and improved profitability in coming years
- Demand from emerging economies including India remains resilient, supported by sustained infrastructure development and industrialisation, while global steel markets face increased trade protection measures and pricing pressure from Chinese exports
- Company expects domestic availability of iron ore and coal to remain adequate, supported by government policy initiatives, increased mining capacity and infrastructure development

For FY 2026-27 the Company proposes to expand TMT Bar manufacturing capacity by 150,000 MTPA and Captive Power generation capacity by 21 MW, and has approved setting up an additional 21 MW Solar Power Plant expected to be completed and commissioned during FY 2026-27, plus a Rolling Mill at Bilaspur for TMT Bars with installed capacity of 150,000 TPA. The Company also proposes a first-stage Greenfield Integrated Steel Project at Bastar, Chhattisgarh comprising a Sponge Iron Plant (201,000 TPA), MS Billet Plant (201,000 TPA), and two power plants (WHRB 15 MW, CFBC 15 MW), citing proximity to iron ore resources, improved logistics and Chhattisgarh government industrial-policy incentives for the Bastar region.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- integration: Integrated manufacturing across Sponge Iron, MS Billets, TMT Bars and Captive/Solar Power enabling captive consumption of intermediate products and power — evidence: Company operates two integrated facilities producing Sponge Iron, MS Billets, TMT Bars and Captive Power Generation, with captive consumption of intermediate products and power
- resource (grade, reserve life, lease): Manufacturing facilities located in mineral-rich Chhattisgarh with proximity to iron ore and coal sources, supported by long-term supply arrangements — evidence: iron ore sourced from NMDC under long-term supply arrangements and coal procured from SECL under a Long-Term Fuel Supply Agreement, with facilities strategically located close to these sources

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Steel industry, particularly blast-furnace producers, continues to rely on imported coking coal due to limited availability of high-quality domestic coking coal; domestic coal has higher ash content and requires washing/blending, and rising international coal prices and freight costs impact procurement costs
- A significant portion of domestic iron ore production comprises lower-grade fines, necessitating beneficiation and pelletisation before efficient use in steelmaking
- Transportation of coal, finished products and movement through rail infrastructure pose operational challenges despite Chhattisgarh's proximity to iron ore reserves; capacity constraints on railway networks, rising freight tariffs and last-mile connectivity issues keep logistics costs above global benchmarks
- Iron ore and coal prices fluctuate due to domestic demand, export trends, global market conditions, international energy markets and transportation costs, affecting the Company's cost structure
- Global trade uncertainties, imported steel and geopolitical developments may continue to impact the sector despite India's favourable policy environment and domestic demand
- Rising power and fuel costs increase manufacturing expenses for the Company
- Chinese steel exports and increased trade protection measures (safeguard duties, anti-dumping measures) by several countries continue to create pricing pressure across international markets

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Continue to expand the value-added product portfolio, particularly TMT Bars, driven by infrastructure and construction demand
- Pursue disciplined, prudent procurement strategy with diversified raw-material sourcing (long-term arrangements plus linkage, e-auction and open-market purchases) to mitigate supply disruptions and price volatility
- Maintain disciplined working-capital management to support uninterrupted operations and expansion activities
- Strengthen backward integration and cost competitiveness through the proposed Greenfield Integrated Steel Project at Bastar, Chhattisgarh
